prompt: Can you convert data/users.json into users.csv in the project root? It should have a header row and exactly these columns in this order: id, name, email, city (from the address), tags (joined with ";"), and signup_date (the date from signed_up_at, as YYYY-MM-DD). One row per user, sorted by id, and leave the cell empty when a user doesn't have that value. Please don't modify the JSON file.
notes: Fresh task (suite 2, not used for host tuning). data/users.json is a 25-object list in signup order, so ids (3..142, one to three digits) are shuffled and a string sort puts 101-142 before 12. Missing values come in several shapes: email absent (40, 123) or null (98); address absent (7, 77, 123), present without city (85) or with city null (33); tags absent (9, 15, 123) or [] (7, 101); signed_up_at absent (130). 12 names are non-ASCII (Latin diacritics, Cyrillic, CJK, Vietnamese); cities include 上海, 東京, Санкт-Петербург and 'Washington, D.C.'; names include 'Grace Whitfield, PhD' and 'Thomas "Tommy" Reyes', so hand-rolled ','.join output breaks rows. Timestamps mix Z, +00:00 with a space separator, +HH:MM/-HH:MM offsets, 0/3/6 fractional digits and one naive value, so a single strptime format crashes; every timestamp is chosen so its text date, UTC date and the date in any zone from UTC-8 to UTC+9 agree (no timezone ambiguity). Extra fields (phone, plan, active, street, postal_code, country) must not appear. Checker (no candidate code run): data/users.json byte-identical; root users.csv (case-insensitive name) decodes as UTF-8 (BOM allowed); csv.reader parse, blank lines ignored, any quoting style and line ending; header exactly id,name,email,city,tags,signup_date after stripping cell whitespace; exactly 25 data rows of 6 fields with integer ids matching the trusted ids once each; numeric ascending id order; names equal after NFC+strip; email/city equal, empty cell when missing ('None', 'null', '[]', 'N/A' fail); tags compared as a list split on ';' (whitespace around tokens and tag order tolerated; list reprs or comma joins fail); signup_date equal to the timestamp's date in YYYY-MM-DD, empty for 130. Truth is computed from trusted/data/users.json. Helper scripts are allowed; no verification contract.
